slides.say: A circle is inscribed in a right triangle whose legs are eight centimeters and fifteen centimeters. What is the radius of the circle, in centimeters?

Inscribed in the triangle means the circle sits inside it and touches all three sides. So every side of the triangle is a tangent to the circle. [short pause] We'll use the tangent rules, and at the end there's a short formula too.

[short pause] Let's start with the math way. Here's the triangle again, bigger. First the third side, the hypotenuse. By Pythagoras, its square is the two legs squared, added together. Eight squared is sixty-four. Fifteen squared is two hundred twenty-five. Together that's two hundred eighty-nine.
Eight, fifteen, seventeen is a Pythagorean triple, and seventeen squared really is two hundred eighty-nine. So the hypotenuse is seventeen.
Now the tangent rule. The sides are tangents, so I draw the radii to the two legs. Each radius is perpendicular to its leg.

So the little corner shape has three right angles, and its fourth angle is a right angle too. Its two sides from the center are radii, so both are r. A rectangle with two equal sides next to each other is a square. So it's a square, r by r, in the corner.
So the corner pieces of the legs are r and r. The rest of the short leg is eight minus r, and the rest of the long leg is fifteen minus r.

Now let's use the second rule. Two tangents from the same point are equal. From the top corner come two tangents, so the top piece of the hypotenuse is also eight minus r. From the bottom corner on the right, the other piece is fifteen minus r.
These two pieces make the whole hypotenuse, seventeen. So eight minus r plus fifteen minus r is seventeen.
Eight plus fifteen is twenty-three, so twenty-three minus two r is seventeen. We want r alone, without the minus. So let's add two r to both sides. Twenty-three is equal to seventeen plus two r.
Now subtract seventeen from both sides. Six is equal to two r. Then divide both sides by two, and r is three. Choice number three is our answer.
at: Six is equal to two r
Choice number three is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Now the math way again, with a short formula. It works for right triangles. Call the legs a and b, and the hypotenuse c. The radius of the circle inside is a plus b minus c, all over two.
at: Call the legs a and b

slides.say: Why does it work? It's our equation again. The leg pieces, a minus r and b minus r, add up to c. So two r is a plus b minus c.
Here, eight plus fifteen minus seventeen is six, and half of six is three. Careful, six is in the choices too. That's someone who forgot to divide by two.
at: someone who forgot to divide by two

slides.say: Let's try it on another right triangle, three, four, five. Three plus four minus five is two, and half of two is one. So the circle inside that triangle has radius one.

And eight and a half is half of the hypotenuse. Remember, in a right triangle the hypotenuse is a diameter of the circle around the triangle, the one through its three corners. So eight and a half is the radius of that outside circle, not of the circle inside. The answer is three, choice number three. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
